description:
BRANCHING-STRATEGY REVIEW (2026-07-06, session on PR #993). `main` is already
release-only: validate-main-pr.yml rejects any PR whose head is not a vX.Y.Z
branch, release-finalize fast-forwards+tags it, and its HEAD is always the
exact latest-release commit. `release` is the accurate name.

This is Decision B — deliberately separated from the low-risk default-branch
switch (Decision A, branch-default-switch-to-develop). Unlike A, B has real
functional blast radius: it touches the release-publish gate, so it is its
own change, sequenced AFTER A (per the session's branch-rename runbook draft,
saved outside the tree).

This item captures the full surface discovered on develop, which is larger
than the curated main branch shows. NO behavioral gain — this is naming
clarity — so priority is Medium.

Verified safe / unchanged (do not touch): PyPI trusted publishing (keyed on
repo + workflow filename release.yml + environment pypi, never a branch);
GitHub Pages (deploy-pages, source = GitHub Actions). README badges pin no
branch.

STATUS 2026-07-10 (reconciliation): the in-repo work (w1-w5) landed on
branch claude/git-branching-strategy-58vxjs as PR #1114 (awaiting Code Owner
review; touches release.yml). A parallel duplicate attempt, PR #1027, was
closed as superseded — #1114 is a strict superset of its file set and folded
in its two correct findings. Two refinements discovered during execution:
(a) default-branch-vs-release-branch classification — RELEASE_CANARY_BRANCH
and seed-corpus.yml's PR base are DEFAULT-branch semantics and go to
`develop`, NOT `release` (the canary fires from the default branch; seed
corpus carries curated-off results-data with a chore/ head); (b) the
protected-branch guards keep `main` blocked during the migration window
(`develop|main|release`), because a stale local `main` can still exist until
the GitHub rename. Only w6 (admin) remains.

anti_patterns.dont: rename the branch (w6) before w1-w5 merge
anti_patterns.instead: land the in-repo edits and the branch rename in one coordinated step.
anti_patterns.why: a half-applied state leaves release-cut opening PRs against a release branch that does not exist

anti_patterns.instead: a token swap there produces wrong docs.
anti_patterns.why: its scheduling/default-branch section encodes GitHub mechanics (scheduled workflows run from the DEFAULT branch) whose truth changes with Decision A

anti_patterns.dont: touch the MAIN_CLONE / 'main clone' worktree-pool concept in the Makefile
anti_patterns.why: it is the primary-checkout notion, unrelated to the branch name.

preserves.behavior: PyPI trusted publishing, the pypi/test-pypi/github-pages environments, and the release.yml filename — all branch-independent; unchanged.
The legitimate release flow (release-cut / release-finalize) keeps working end-to-end after the rename — every main reference in those targets moves atomically.
release.yml verify-tag-on-* gate and the tag-shaped-ref publish condition — the rename must not loosen the publish gate; only retarget main->release.

_project/decisions/single-repo-migration.md — the architecture record for the two-branch flow; the branching-strategy decision (A+B) should be recorded here or as a sibling decision doc (w5).
docs/operations/branch-rename-runbook.md — COMMITTED in PR #1114 (w4); enumerates the full admin sequence, ordering/no-gap reasoning, verification, and rollback. This is the runbook for w6.

`gh api -X POST repos/joeharris76/BenchBox/branches/main/rename
-f new_name=release` (GitHub redirects old URLs, retargets open PRs).
Recreate the main-release-only ruleset as release-only on
